messages:
sam: Quick bring-up note for Mercantile's LoRA (mercantile-lora-1). Ran a 25-prompt quickpack focused on invoices + an extended 60-case stress set. Artifacts: base(redwood/xl-7b fp16), mercantile-lora-1 fp16 merge, and quant targets int8 and int4 (blockwise). High-level: int8 fine; int4 introduces three distinct quirks we should triage.
olivia: what quirks?
sam: 1) trailing-cent loss (e.g. expected "$1,200.00" -> "1200 dollars" or "1.2K"), 2) special-prefix token aliasing (Mercantile uses tokens like `AMT:`, `ORD#`), 3) occasional hyphen-splitting on order IDs which breaks downstream regex parsers.
devin: numbers pls (quickpack aggregated).
sam: short table below (quickpack + stress):

```
model                           EM   F1   numeric_halluc  fmt_mismatch  mean_tok_l2_delta
redwood/xl-7b_fp16 (base)       87%  92%  1.4%            2/250         0.0000
mercantile-lora-1_fp16          88%  93%  1.2%            1/250         0.0013
mercantile-lora-1_int8          87%  92%  1.7%            3/250         0.0045
mercantile-lora-1_int4          81%  88%  7.1%           17/250         0.0302
```

notes: numeric_halluc includes dropped cents and invented currency words; fmt_mismatch counts canonical formatting diffs vs expected.
maria: tokenization check on `AMT:` / `ORD#`?
sam: yesint8 preserves them. int4 increases embedding distance for those tokens (AMT: delta=0.036, ORD# delta=0.028). Also saw `,` and `.` moved in embedding space (comma delta=0.033).
devin: pipeline used? merge-first quant?
sam: merge -> clip -> quant using blockwise4 group=128 calib=1024 (standard pipeline). snippet: 
```
commit: e12f3a
merge_cmd: tools/merge_lora --base redwood/xl-7b --lora mercantile-lora-1 --out /tmp/mercantile-merged
clip_cmd: python tools/clip_small_weights.py /tmp/mercantile-merged --thresh 1e-4
quant_cmd: tools/quantize --model /tmp/mercantile-merged --bits 4 --group 128 --calib 1024 --method blockwise
```

olivia: given the token deltas, two potential mitigations: A) quantize base first then graft LoRA (apply adapter weights on quant base), B) per-token logit surgery / bias map for numeric/currency tokens during decode, C) explore alternate quant method (smoothquant / gptq) or smaller group sizes.
maria: also think about re-running calibration with more numeric-centric calibration samples (include lots of currency formats). that can help blockwise scales for numeric tokens.
devin: I can run three experiments tonight: (1) graft-on-quant (quant base then apply LoRA), (2) merge-then-quant but group=64 + calib=4096 + include numeric calibration set, (3) merge-then-quant + post-quant logit-bias map keyed to top-40 numeric/currency tokens.
qa-bot: queued extended quickpack for the three variants. Blocking criteria: numeric_halluc > 3.5% OR fmt_mismatch > 10/250. Current int4 baseline = 17/250 -> block.
deploy-bot: Promotion blocked for `mercantile-lora-1_int4`. Promotion flag set: blocked.
olivia: small extra note: Mercantile's downstream parser tolerates "1,200" and "1200" but not "1.2K" or spelled-out words. If any variant produces shorthand abbreviations we should flag as high-severity.
sam: good point. QA: we'll add an additional 40 prompts with shorthand/abbrev cases and negative/parentheses amounts to stress.
maria: I'll prototype a tiny per-token logit-nudge util (scale ~[-0.2, +0.2]) to clamp outputs towards numeric tokens; will validate against held-out set to avoid false positives. ETA EOD.
devin: I'll post runs + kernel logs here in the AM. if streaming fallbacks appear, include trace ids.
olivia: thanks everyone. reproduction command for local: 
```
# reproduce locally
git checkout e12f3a
python tools/run_quickpack.py --model /tmp/mercantile-merged --prompts evals/mercantile-invoices-25.json --out quickruns/1772468014
```

sam: reconvene after the three experiment runs. tagging @deploy-bot: keep promotions blocked for int4 until follow-up. :no_entry_sign:
